subject: System Design
title: Version-Based Cache Keys
description: A fast breakdown of Version-Based Cache Keys for builders.

hook.text: Instead of invalidating a cache key, change the key itself. Old key dies naturally; new key fetches fresh data.

buildup.text: Append a version or hash to cache keys: user:42:v3 instead of user:42. Bump the version on changes.

discovery.text: This avoids invalidation entirely. The old entry expires via TTL; the new version is a fresh cache miss.

twist.text: You still need to store the current version somewhere. If that lookup is slow, you've moved the problem, not solved it.

climax.text: Version-based keys are elegant for cache layers where direct invalidation is impossible, like CDNs.

punchline.text: Don't delete old keys — just stop asking for them.

quiz.question: How do version-based cache keys work?
options: The key includes a version that changes on updates, making old keys unused
Keys are encrypted with a version number
